_metadata.disclaimer: All values are best estimates based on published research, corporate sustainability reports, and peer-reviewed studies. Where data is unavailable, reasonable assumptions are noted. We welcome corrections and better data.

primary_sources.title: Making AI Less Thirsty: Uncovering and Addressing the Secret Water Footprint of AI Models
primary_sources.authors: Pengfei Li, Jianyi Yang, Mohammad A. Islam, Shaolei Ren

primary_sources.title: 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report
The carbon footprint of streaming video: fact-checking the headlines
What is the environmental footprint for social media applications? 2021 Edition
Carbon Footprint of Digital Activities Study
Water Use Requirements for Data Centers in Texas
primary_sources.institution: COMPASS Research Consortium, Bureau of Economic Geology, UT Austin

primary_sources.title: Tracking electricity consumption from U.S. cryptocurrency mining operations
Fact Sheet — Energy and Water Use in the U.S. Electric Grid
primary_sources.institution: Environmental and Energy Study Institute (EESI), analysis of LBNL and EIA data
primary_sources.notes: US national average grid water consumption: 4.54 L/kWh (1.2 gal/kWh). Used as default gridWaterIntensity.

wue_by_provider._description: Water Usage Effectiveness: liters of water consumed for cooling per kWh of IT energy. Lower = better. Industry average is ~1.8 L/kWh.

industry_average.notes: Widely cited benchmark; includes older and less efficient facilities

arizona.notes: Arid climate requires heavy cooling; pilot zero-water facility planned 2026

sweden_finland.notes: Cold climates require minimal cooling; estimated from Microsoft descriptions

iowa.notes: Estimated from fleet average and climate data

virginia.notes: Large cluster; improving as new builds come online

netherlands.notes: Cool climate allows extensive free cooling

future_target.timeline: New designs from Aug 2024, operational late 2027
future_target.notes: Zero-water evaporation cooling using closed-loop chip-level cooling. Saves 125M+ liters per datacenter per year.

global_average.notes: Google reports PUE (1.09 in 2024) but is less transparent about WUE by region. Estimated from total water consumption and energy data.

google.notes: Replenished 64% (4.5B gallons) via water stewardship projects in 2024, though methodology is disputed

global_average.notes: AWS claims 0.15 L/kWh but has not disclosed total water consumption. Some investigations suggest significantly higher actual use.

recent_builds.notes: Recently completed facilities; 80% more efficient than their older portfolio average

energy_per_activity._description: Estimated energy consumption per unit of digital activity. These are data-center-side estimates unless noted otherwise.

chatgpt_single_query.source: Multiple estimates converging; ~10x a Google search
chatgpt_single_query.notes: Varies significantly by model size. GPT-4 likely higher than GPT-3.5. Range: 0.2-10 Wh depending on model and response length.

chatgpt_conversation_20_50_queries.notes: Basis for the widely-cited '500mL per conversation' estimate

google_gemini_text_query.notes: Google's own estimate; significantly lower than third-party ChatGPT estimates

ai_image_generation.notes: Highly variable by model (DALL-E, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion) and resolution

ai_video_generation_5sec.notes: Extremely energy-intensive; ~1 kWh for 5 seconds of video. Limited data available.

google_search.source: Google (2009, likely lower now due to efficiency gains)
google_search.notes: Widely cited figure. Google says efficiency has improved but hasn't published updated number.

google_ai_overview_search.notes: AI-augmented search results require additional inference compute

streaming_video._notes: Includes data center, CDN, and network transmission. Does NOT include user device energy unless noted.

netflix_hd_per_hour.notes: IEA 2020 estimate for HD streaming. Includes data center + network. Device energy adds 0.02-0.1 kWh depending on screen.

youtube_hd_per_hour.notes: YouTube has different CDN architecture but comparable bitrates for HD

youtube_sd_per_hour.notes: SD uses roughly half the data of HD

tiktok_per_hour.source: Estimated; short-form video with heavy recommendation compute
tiktok_per_hour.notes: TikTok's recommendation algorithm adds server-side compute cost beyond pure streaming

zoom_video_call_per_hour.source: Various estimates; 0.5-1.0 kWh including device for group calls
zoom_video_call_per_hour.notes: Highly variable: 1-on-1 vs group, video on/off, resolution. 0.15 kWh is server-side for typical 1-on-1.

social_media._notes: Per-minute energy consumption on the device side (phone). Server-side costs are additional.

tiktok_scroll_per_minute.notes: Highest energy consumer among social apps measured

twitter_scroll_per_minute.notes: Lower data exchange than video-heavy platforms

regular_email.notes: Without attachments. Attachments can increase 10x or more.

cloud_gaming_per_hour.source: Estimated; cloud gaming requires continuous GPU rendering server-side
cloud_gaming_per_hour.notes: Highly variable by platform (GeForce Now, Xbox Cloud, PS Now) and game complexity

console_gaming_per_hour_device_only.notes: PS5/Xbox Series X ~100-200W during active gaming. This is device only, not server-side.

mobile_gaming_per_hour.notes: Phone draws ~3-8W during gaming; server costs for online games are additional

bitcoin_transaction.source: Digiconomist / Cambridge Bitcoin Electricity Consumption Index
bitcoin_transaction.notes: Extremely energy-intensive due to proof-of-work. One transaction ≈ avg US household for 24 days.

device_energy._description: Energy consumption of user devices during digital activities. Important for total water footprint calculation.

smartphone_active_use_per_hour.notes: Varies by screen brightness, processing load. Range: 3-8W

laptop_active_per_hour.notes: Range: 30-80W depending on model and workload

desktop_pc_per_hour.notes: Range: 80-300W. Gaming PCs at high end.

tv_55_inch_led_per_hour.notes: Modern LED TVs: 50-120W. OLED may be slightly higher.

gaming_console_active_per_hour.notes: PS5: ~100-200W active. Xbox Series X similar.

wifi_router_per_hour.notes: Always-on device; contributes to all network activities

water_per_activity_calculated._description: Pre-calculated water cost estimates using the calculation chain: kWh × WUE = liters. These use the industry average WUE (1.8 L/kWh) as the default, with regional variations available via the multipliers table.

chatgpt_single_query.range_notes: Low end: efficient model + cold-climate DC. High end: large model + hot-climate DC.

chatgpt_conversation_20_50_queries.calculation: Widely cited figure from Ren et al. (2023) for 20-50 exchanges

ai_video_generation_5sec.comparison: Almost 4 standard water bottles for 5 seconds of AI video

netflix_1_hour_hd.comparison: About half a glass of water

netflix_1_hour_hd_with_tv.notes: Including a 55-inch LED TV's power consumption
netflix_1_hour_hd_with_tv.comparison: Just over one glass of water

tiktok_1_hour.notes: Higher due to recommendation algorithm compute

zoom_1_hour_video.notes: Server + laptop. Group calls can be significantly higher.

cloud_gaming_1_hour.comparison: More than a standard water bottle per hour

console_gaming_1_hour_offline.notes: Device power only; grid electricity generation also uses water

one_bitcoin_transaction.comparison: Equivalent to about 8 full bathtubs of water

regional_multipliers._description: Multipliers to adjust the default (industry average) water cost by region. Based on WUE data and climate factors. Multiply the default water estimate by this factor.

us_southwest_arizona.notes: Despite Microsoft's high WUE here, many DCs use heavy evaporative cooling. Water stress is extreme.

us_virginia.notes: Largest US DC cluster (Data Center Alley). Humidity reduces but doesn't eliminate cooling water needs.

us_iowa.notes: Cold winters allow free cooling part of year. Major Microsoft and Google presence.

us_texas_san_antonio.notes: Rapidly expanding DC market. Water availability is a growing concern. SAWS service area.

us_oregon.notes: Cool climate, access to hydroelectric power. Major Google, Facebook, Amazon presence.

nordics_sweden_finland.notes: Near-zero cooling water needs for much of the year. Abundant renewable energy.

ireland.notes: Temperate climate reduces cooling needs. Major EU DC hub but facing grid capacity issues.

netherlands.notes: Cool climate, major European DC hub.

singapore.notes: Despite hot climate, advanced cooling tech and reclaimed water bring WUE very low.

middle_east_uae.notes: Extreme cooling demands. Often uses desalinated water, which itself is energy-intensive.

india_mumbai.notes: Growing DC market. High cooling demands, variable water availability.

comparisons_library._description: Relatable real-world comparisons for water quantities. Used to make results tangible.

meta_calculation._description: How to calculate the water cost of using THIS tool (the meta layer). Based on the Anthropic Claude API.

estimated_wh_per_1000_tokens.source: Extrapolated from published LLM energy estimates. Claude Sonnet likely in the 0.1-0.5 Wh per 1000 token range.
estimated_wh_per_1000_tokens.notes: This is a rough estimate. Anthropic has not published per-query energy data. We use a conservative mid-range estimate.

average_query_tokens.notes: Rough average for a typical Q&A interaction on this tool

estimated_water_per_tool_query_ml.notes: Very small per query, but it adds up across millions of users

training_water_costs._description: One-time water costs for training AI models. Amortized across all queries over the model's lifetime.

gpt3_training.notes: 700,000 liters of freshwater evaporated training GPT-3 in Microsoft US data centers

gpt4_training.notes: No official figures. Estimated based on compute scaling.

global_ai_water_projection_2027.notes: More than the total annual water withdrawal of 4-6 Denmark or half the UK

indirect_water_costs._description: Water used in electricity GENERATION (scope-2), not at the data center. Often larger than on-site cooling water but rarely discussed.

thermoelectric_power_water_per_kwh_liter.notes: Cooling water for power plants. This is IN ADDITION to data center WUE.

renewable_water_per_kwh_liters.notes: Solar panels need cleaning; wind is near-zero. Hydro reservoirs lose water to evaporation.

indirect_water_costs.notes: On average, generating 1 kWh of US grid electricity withdraws ~1.8 liters of water. This roughly DOUBLES the total water footprint when added to on-site DC cooling.
